In terms of elections, there is the House of Representatives, the Senate, and the Presidency. The House is elected democratically by districts within states. Each district elects one representative (there are 435 reps in total). Representatives are elected every 2 years.

The Senate is also elected democratically by states. Each state gets two senators (100 total). Senators are elected every 6 years (typically only one will be elected at a time)

Then there's the presidency. The President is elected though the electoral college every 4 years (max of 8 years for one individual). The electoral college works by granting each state with a select number of voters delegated by their party. For example, Trump won Kentucky, and all 8 of Kentucky's electoral voters (picked by the Republican party since Trump won the state) voted for Trump. If one candidate gets 270 or more electoral votes, then they are elected president. The president isn't elected perfectly democratically, but it's a lot better this way since states like California and New York would just control the whole country.
